chunks: A man came while he was in the presence of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), and he was informed of a newborn that had arrived for him. The face of the man changed. The Prophet (peace be upon him) said to him: 'What is the matter with you?' He said, 'Nothing.' He said, 'Speak.' He said, 'I went out while the woman was in labour, and I was informed that she had given birth to a girl.' The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said to him: 'The earth will carry her, the sky will shade her, God will provide for her, and she is a fragrant flower you will smell.'

key_terms.تَمْخَضُ: to be in the throes of labour — from the root م-خ-ض referring to the churning motion of labour
key_terms.جَارِيَة: girl/daughter — in classical Arabic, can mean a girl, a young woman, or a female slave; here used in the sense of a newborn daughter
key_terms.رَيْحَانَة: sweet basil or fragrant herb — used metaphorically to describe a daughter as a source of joy, beauty, and sweetness
key_terms.يَرْفَعُهُ: he raises it (mursal chain marker) — indicates Hamza ibn Humran traced this narration back without specifying each intermediary

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say about the birth of a daughter in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates an encounter in which a man's visible distress upon learning his wife had given birth to a girl was directly addressed by the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW). The Prophet rebuked the pre-Islamic cultural attitude of disappointment at daughters by presenting a beautiful, poetic vision: the newborn girl is sustained by the earth, sheltered by the sky, provided for by God, and is a fragrant flower for her father to cherish. This teaching was directed at an audience steeped in Jahiliyya-era customs where the birth of daughters was considered a misfortune, as referenced in Quran 16:58-59.
